item.title: Preview: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Is More Of The Same, But Better

description.p: Wuhu Island: Be there or be (Spocco) Square.Back what seems like a lifetime ago, I got a chance to have a pop at Nintendo Switch Sports Resort at gamescom '26. No, I don’t mean the stuff that just anyone with a ticket and the patience to wait in an enormous queue could play. No, I got a chance to play sports that the average Joes could only dream of, like table tennis.I played prop plane, table tennis, archery, thumb wrestling, skateboarding, bowling, and boxing, but not necessarily in that order. I believe people with the patience to tackle the game on the show floor had the chance to play power cruising (discount Wave Race to you and me), and it’s possible I had the option between that and bowling, if my memory’s correct.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: "I Wanted To Challenge Myself" - Former WarioWare Director Talks Life After Nintendo

description.p: Wario Where?Earlier this year, Nintendo veteran and WarioWare legend Goro Abe announced that he was leaving the company and taking up a teaching post at the Osaka Electro-Communication University. Roughly seven months on, VGC got the chance to chat with the dev about his post-Nintendo life, and, rather expectedly, games are still very much on his mind.“Making games takes a lot of time, and I knew that based on my age and career that I could not make that many more games in the future,” Abe told VGC. “And I wanted to challenge myself to do other stuff. So I thought it would be interesting to do things that I had never done before, and that’s why I decided to go into teaching.”Read the full article on nintendolife.com
